# ulmBLAS benchmark results

This directory archives benchmark campaigns of ulmBLAS: measurements of the
micro kernels and of the BLAS routines on specific hardware, compared with
other BLAS implementations.  Every campaign documents its hardware, software,
source revisions and methodology, contains the raw measurements and the
scripts that generate its figures, so that results remain comparable when
new micro kernels are added or other hardware becomes available.

## Structure of a campaign

A campaign is a directory `DATE-MACHINE-EXPERIMENT` (e.g.
`2026-10-24-heim-avx-fma`) with

| File or directory | Contents |
|-------------------|----------|
| `campaign.conf`   | metadata used for the index: `NAME`, `DATE`, `MACHINE`, `TITLE`, `SUMMARY` (`KEY = value` lines) |
| `README.md`       | experiment, hardware, software, methodology, results and conclusions |
| `data/`           | measurements as CSV files (raw outputs of the benchmark programs may be kept in `data/raw/`) |
| `plots/`          | Gnuplot scripts (`*.gp`, scripts starting with `_` are only loaded by others) and the SVG figures they generate |
| `source/`         | the benchmark programs and scripts that produced the data |

Compiled programs, object files, libraries and other build artifacts are not
archived.

## Adding a campaign

After a benchmark campaign is completed (the archive does not run
benchmarks), prepare a campaign directory as described above, then run

    make add_benchmark_result BENCHMARK_DIR=path/to/campaign [BENCHMARK_NAME=name]

`BENCHMARK_NAME` is optional; if given, it must equal `NAME` in
`campaign.conf`.  The target

1. validates the campaign: metadata (the name must start with the date),
   `README.md`, at least one CSV file with measurements, at least one plot
   script, no binaries or build artifacts;
2. generates all figures with Gnuplot (an error if Gnuplot or its SVG
   terminal is missing; `GNUPLOT=...` selects the program) and checks the
   SVG files;
3. updates the list of figures in the campaign's `README.md` (between
   `<!-- BEGIN FIGURES -->` and `<!-- END FIGURES -->`, appended if missing);
4. copies the campaign to `benchmark_results/NAME` and regenerates the index
   above from the `campaign.conf` files of all campaigns.

Nothing in `benchmark_results/` changes unless all steps succeed.  Archived
campaigns are never overwritten with different data: adding a campaign that
is already archived with the same contents only regenerates its figures
(no duplicate entries); different contents under an existing name are
rejected.  To regenerate the figures of an archived campaign, use it as
`BENCHMARK_DIR` (e.g. `BENCHMARK_DIR=benchmark_results/2026-10-24-heim-avx-fma`).
The target is independent of the library build and of `make check`, and it
neither commits nor publishes anything.
